Exploratory notebook. Can the Bayesian sequential-sampling model of Frömer,
Callaway, Griffiths & Shenhav (2025, *Open Mind*), extended to attributes,
explain the range-sensitive and reference-dependent attention weights in the
paper? Nothing here is in the paper yet.

The notebook is written so that, if the results hold up, its sections can be
moved into `Main_Analysis.Rmd` by cut-and-paste. The first section copies the
main notebook's preamble, data chunks and plot helpers (delete those copies
when porting; the data cleaning itself already lives in
`code/utilities/build_boxlong.R`, which the main notebook can switch to). Everything
model-specific lives in scripts under `code/`:

- `code/simulation/simulate_bayesian_attributes.R`: the model and its closed-form choice probabilities
- `code/fitting/fit_bayesian_attributes.R`: maximum-likelihood fitting, leave-one-out, the list of variants
- `code/fitting/run_bayesian_fits.R`: fits every variant and runs the leave-one-out from a terminal (every fold is a full refit, so hours; see the script header), caching to `results/cache/bayesian_model/`
- `code/parameter_recovery/recover_bayesian_attributes.R`: parameter recovery for the main model, from a terminal (~1.5 hours)

This notebook loads those caches. With `RUN_FITS <- TRUE` it fits any variant
whose cache is missing (slow); with `FALSE` it skips it.

Sections:

1. Copied preamble and data
2. Model
3. Sanity checks
4. Parameter recovery
5. Fits and leave-one-out
6. Out-of-sample attention weights: main and supplementary figures, tables
7. Notes

```{r flex-design}
# Design matrix for the cell-weight regression (the main notebook's
# flex-design chunk, generalized). `bl` is box-level data and `ps` trial-level
# data; both need a `TrialKey` column (Trial for the real data; Trial_rep for
# simulated data, where every rep of a trial counts as a new trial) and a
# `ChooseL` column. Returns one row per trial: ChooseL, Study, the three
# signed value channels SV_P / SV_N / SV_B, and the signed dwell in every
# (type x value) cell (0 where the cell wasn't on screen).
build_flex_dat <- function(range, bl, ps) {
  bl <- bl %>% filter(WN == range)
  ps <- ps %>% filter(WN == range)

  flex_design <- bl %>%
    group_by(Subject, TrialKey, cell) %>%
    summarise(sd = sum(signed_dwell), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = cell, values_from = sd, values_fill = 0)

  value_design <- bl %>%
    group_by(Subject, TrialKey, type) %>%
    summarise(SV = sum(signed_value), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = SV, names_prefix = "SV_", values_fill = 0)

  ps %>%
    transmute(Subject, TrialKey, ChooseL, Study = factor(Study)) %>%
    left_join(value_design, by = c("Subject", "TrialKey")) %>%
    left_join(flex_design,  by = c("Subject", "TrialKey"))
}
```

```{r plot-weights}
# Signed attention weights by type and value, Narrow and Wide overlaid (the
# main notebook's plot_weights_by_range, plus a `ylim` argument; NULL = free).
plot_weights_by_range <- function(weights, title, ylim = c(-0.5, 0.5)) {
  p <- ggplot(weights, aes(x = value, y = estimate, color = WN, shape = WN)) +
    facet_wrap(~ type, scales = "free_x", labeller = type_labels) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50") +
    geom_line(linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), size = pt_size, linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
    wn_scales +
    labs(x = "Attribute Value", y = "Attention Weight", title = title) +
    .myPlot + type_strip_style + study_title + legend_right + theme(legend.direction = "vertical") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = x_attr_breaks)
  if (!is.null(ylim)) p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim)
  p
}
```

```{r data-weights}
# The data's cell weights: posterior medians and 95% HDIs from the two cached
# brms fits (the main notebook's flex-summary chunk). Each fit is ~900 MB, so
# the summary is cached after the first extraction.
data_weights_file <- file.path(cache_dir, "data_cell_weights.rds")
if (file.exists(data_weights_file)) {
  weights_data <- readRDS(data_weights_file)
} else {
  weights_data <- tibble()
  for (rng in c("Narrow", "Wide")) {
    f <- file.path(fit_dir, paste0("flex_attention_weights_pooled_", tolower(rng), ".rds"))
    if (!file.exists(f)) { cat("No cached fit", f, "\n"); next }
    draws <- as_draws_df(readRDS(f), variable = "^b_", regex = TRUE)
    cells <- names(draws) %>% str_subset("^b_[PNB]_(neg|pos)[0-9]+$") %>% str_remove("^b_")
    for (s in 1:2) {
      for (cell in cells) {
        # Study 1 is the reference level; Study 2 adds the cell's Study 2 interaction.
        x <- draws[[paste0("b_", cell)]]
        if (s == 2) x <- x + draws[[paste0("b_", cell, ":Study2")]]
        h <- bayestestR::hdi(x, ci = 0.95)
        weights_data <- bind_rows(weights_data, tibble(
          Study = s, WN = rng, term = cell, estimate = median(x), lo = h$CI_low, hi = h$CI_high
        ))
      }
    }
    rm(draws); invisible(gc())
  }
  if (nrow(weights_data) > 0) {
    weights_data <- weights_data %>% mutate(
      type  = factor(str_sub(term, 1, 1), levels = c("N", "B", "P")),
      value = as.numeric(str_extract(term, "[0-9]+$")) * if_else(str_detect(term, "_neg"), -1, 1),
      WN    = factor(WN, levels = c("Narrow", "Wide"))
    )
    saveRDS(weights_data, data_weights_file)
  }
}
```

---

# Model

Every box (option x attribute) is an item whose value the participant
estimates by sampling while the box is hovered. The estimate starts at a prior
mean and moves toward what was seen; how far it moves depends on how long the
box was looked at and on how noisy looking is. This is Frömer et al.'s model
with two changes: the items are attributes, and an option's value is the sum of
its two attribute estimates, each valued relative to the prior mean with loss
aversion.

**Where the range enters.** A box is measured against a reference distribution
with mean $\mu_D$, SD $s_D$, minimum and maximum. The prior reference is either
the six values the box's attribute type can take in the participant's range
condition (one prior per type x range) or all eighteen values of the range
condition (one prior per range, shared by P, N and B). Values and noise are in
points for every current variant. Because every subject is in one range
condition and has their own noise, differences in noise between conditions are
absorbed by the subjects' $\sigma$ whatever the units are, so the units only
matter for how the attribute types are weighted within a condition; an earlier
round of fits showed that weighting per point beats weighting by each type's
spread, which is why only points are kept.

**Prior.** $\mathcal{N}(m_0, s_p^2)$: $m_0$ sits a fraction $q$ of the way from
the reference's minimum to its maximum ($q = 0.5$ is the middle), and
$s_p = s_D$, the spread of the reference. (An earlier round fitted the ratio
$s_p / s_D$ freely and found 1.07 and 1.17, so it is now fixed at 1.) The zero
prior fixes $m_0$ at an objective 0, which for the symmetric spans of this
design is $q = 0.5$; the flat prior keeps that mean and sets $s_p$ to 1000
$s_D$, so the prior carries no weight in the estimate, but its mean still
serves as the reference of the loss-aversion kink below.

**Sampling and loss aversion.** For a box with value $a$ after $t$ seconds of dwell,

$$
w = \frac{t / \sigma^2}{1 / s_p^2 + t / \sigma^2}, \qquad
m = m_0 + w\,(\bar{x} - m_0), \quad \bar{x} \sim \mathcal{N}(a, \sigma^2 / t),
$$

and the box is valued relative to the prior mean with a kink,
$u(m) = m_0 + (m - m_0)$ if $m \ge m_0$ and $u(m) = m_0 + \lambda (m - m_0)$ if
$m < m_0$. With $\lambda > 1$ attention repels more strongly from a box whose
estimate sits below the reference than it attracts toward one above it;
$\lambda = 1$ is the plain model. An option's estimate is the sum of its two
boxes' $u(m)$; the larger one is chosen. Given the dwell times each $m$ is
normal, the mean and variance of $u(m)$ have closed forms (partial moments of a
normal around the kink), and $V_L - V_R$ is treated as normal with the summed
mean and variance, so the probability of choosing left is a probit. The sanity
checks compare this closed form with a box-by-box simulation. Trials with a box
that was never hovered (NA dwell) are dropped, as the paper's regressions drop them.

**Parameters and error model.** $\sigma$ (noise per second, one per subject);
$q$ per range condition; $\lambda$ shared by both conditions (the
`cond_lamcond` variant fits it per condition as a check). All group parameters
are pooled across subjects. One algorithm fits every variant, and the variants
differ only in which group parameters are free: the zero and flat priors fix
$q$ at 0.5 and fit $\sigma$ and $\lambda$ like the others. The subjects' log
noise values are partially pooled, with a Gaussian pull toward the group median
(SD of one log unit), the same logic as a subject random effect; it only bites
for subjects whose 30 or 60 trials leave $\sigma$ poorly determined, and it
keeps a held-out error from ever costing more than a few log-likelihood units.

**Variants.** `cond_lam` (per-condition prior, loss aversion), `cond_lam1`
(same, $\lambda = 1$), `type_lam` and `type_lam1` (per-type prior with and
without loss aversion), `cond_lamcond` ($\lambda$ per condition), `zero`
(prior mean at an objective 0, Frömer et al.'s ZERO PRIOR, with loss aversion
around it) and `flat` (no pull toward a prior, loss aversion around 0). The
paper's comparison table carries `cond_lam`, `cond_lam1`, `type_lam`, `zero`
and `flat`.

```{r model-source}
source(here::here("code/simulation/simulate_bayesian_attributes.R"))
source(here::here("code/fitting/fit_bayesian_attributes.R"))
variants <- bayesian_variants()
str(variants, max.level = 1)
```

```{r model-helpers}
# Cell-weight regression by plain logistic regression (no random effects, as
# Frömer et al. did for simulated data), one fit per range condition and
# study. `bl` and `ps` need TrialKey and ChooseL columns (see build_flex_dat).
# Returns the cell weights and the three value slopes, with Wald 95% CIs.
cell_weight_glm <- function(bl, ps) {
  weights <- tibble()
  slopes  <- tibble()
  for (rng in c("Narrow", "Wide")) {
    dat   <- build_flex_dat(rng, bl, ps)
    cells <- setdiff(names(dat), c("Subject", "TrialKey", "ChooseL", "Study", "SV_P", "SV_N", "SV_B"))
    f     <- as.formula(paste("ChooseL ~ SV_P + SV_N + SV_B +", paste(cells, collapse = " + ")))
    for (s in 1:2) {
      fit <- glm(f, family = binomial, data = dat %>% filter(Study == s))
      co  <- summary(fit)$coefficients
      est <- tibble(term = rownames(co), estimate = co[, 1], se = co[, 2]) %>%
        mutate(lo = estimate - 1.96 * se, hi = estimate + 1.96 * se, Study = s, WN = rng)
      weights <- bind_rows(weights, est %>% filter(term %in% cells))
      slopes  <- bind_rows(slopes,  est %>% filter(str_starts(term, "SV_")))
    }
  }
  weights <- weights %>% mutate(
    type  = factor(str_sub(term, 1, 1), levels = c("N", "B", "P")),
    value = as.numeric(str_extract(term, "[0-9]+$")) * if_else(str_detect(term, "_neg"), -1, 1),
    WN    = factor(WN, levels = c("Narrow", "Wide"))
  )
  slopes <- slopes %>% mutate(
    type = factor(str_remove(term, "SV_"), levels = c("N", "B", "P")),
    WN   = factor(WN, levels = c("Narrow", "Wide"))
  )
  list(weights = weights, slopes = slopes)
}

# Simulated choices -> attention weights. `trials` needs Subject, Trial, WN,
# Study and p_left (the model's probability of choosing left). Every rep of a
# trial is treated as a new trial (TrialKey = Trial_rep).
simulated_weights <- function(trials, reps = 10, seed = 1) {
  sims <- simulate_choices_from_prob(trials, reps, seed) %>%
    transmute(Subject, Trial, WN, Study, TrialKey = Trial_rep, ChooseL = ChooseL_sim)
  bl_sim <- boxlong %>% select(-ChooseL) %>%
    inner_join(sims %>% select(Subject, Trial, TrialKey, ChooseL), by = c("Subject", "Trial"),
               relationship = "many-to-many")   # 4 boxes x reps per trial
  cell_weight_glm(bl_sim, sims)
}

# Where a type's attention weights cross zero, as a fraction of the way from
# the type's minimum to its maximum value (linear interpolation between the
# first adjacent pair that goes from negative to positive). "all+" / "all-"
# when the weights never change sign.
crossover <- function(values, weights) {
  o <- order(values); a <- values[o]; w <- weights[o]
  if (all(w >= 0)) return("all+")
  if (all(w <  0)) return("all-")
  for (i in seq_len(length(a) - 1)) {
    if (w[i] < 0 && w[i + 1] >= 0) {
      x0 <- a[i] + (a[i + 1] - a[i]) * (-w[i]) / (w[i + 1] - w[i])
      return(sprintf("%.2f", (x0 - min(a)) / (max(a) - min(a))))
    }
  }
  "mixed"
}

# Crossover of every (Study, range, type) in a weights table.
crossover_table <- function(weights, source) {
  out <- tibble()
  for (s in 1:2) for (rng in c("Narrow", "Wide")) for (tt in c("N", "B", "P")) {
    w <- weights %>% filter(Study == s, WN == rng, type == tt)
    if (nrow(w) == 0) next
    out <- bind_rows(out, tibble(source = source, Study = s, WN = rng, type = tt, crossover = crossover(w$value, w$estimate)))
  }
  out
}
```

# Sanity checks

The reference distributions, and three checks of the code: the closed-form
choice probabilities against a box-by-box simulation, with and without loss
aversion; a model with almost no noise chooses the better option almost always;
and the sign patterns the variants produce when run through the cell-weight
regression, including a hand-set loss-averse version that shows what a
$\lambda$ of 2.5 does to the bottom of the N range.

One thing to know before reading the sign patterns. The regression attributes
to a cell the effect of dwelling on it, holding the value channels constant.
In the model, dwell does two things: it moves the estimate from the prior mean
toward the true value (the reference-dependent part, proportional to
$z - m_0$), and it makes the estimate more precise. More precision pushes the
choice toward whichever option is truly better, and which option is truly
better is correlated with the attended cell's own value, so even the **flat
prior produces value-dependent cell weights** in this regression, rising with
the cell's value and crossing zero inside each type's range. A cell weight is
therefore not a pure read-out of the prior position: the flat prior sets the
baseline that the prior adds to. The zero prior shifts the N weights down and
the P weights up from that baseline; a per-type prior at $q = 0.5$ adds a
flip at the middle of each type's range.

```{r sanity-reference}
as.data.frame(reference_distributions(boxlong, "type"))
as.data.frame(reference_distributions(boxlong, "cond"))
```

```{r sanity-closed-form}
prep_cond <- prepare_boxes(boxlong, variants$cond_lam)
sig_five  <- setNames(rep(5, nrow(prep_cond$subjects)), prep_cond$subjects$Subject)   # 5 points per second
par_plain <- list(s0 = c(Narrow = 1, Wide = 1), q = c(Narrow = 0.14, Wide = 0.14), lambda = c(Narrow = 1, Wide = 1))
par_loss  <- list(s0 = c(Narrow = 1, Wide = 1), q = c(Narrow = 0.14, Wide = 0.14), lambda = c(Narrow = 2.5, Wide = 2.5))

for (nm in c("lambda = 1", "lambda = 2.5")) {
  par <- if (nm == "lambda = 1") par_plain else par_loss
  pr  <- choice_probabilities(prep_cond, sig_five, par)
  sim_mean <- rep(0, nrow(pr))
  for (i in 1:40) sim_mean <- sim_mean + simulate_choices_direct(prep_cond, sig_five, par, seed = i)$ChooseL_sim
  sim_mean <- sim_mean / 40
  bins <- cut(pr$p_left, seq(0, 1, 0.1), include.lowest = TRUE)
  cat("\n==", nm, "== closed form vs box-by-box simulation, by decile of predicted probability\n")
  print(round(rbind(closed_form = tapply(pr$p_left, bins, mean), simulated = tapply(sim_mean, bins, mean)), 3))
}

# Almost no noise: accuracy on trials with unequal option values should be ~1.
pr0 <- choice_probabilities(prep_cond, setNames(rep(0.05, length(sig_five)), names(sig_five)), par_plain) %>%
  left_join(pas %>% select(Subject, Trial, Diff), by = c("Subject", "Trial"))
cat("\naccuracy with sigma = 0.05 points/s:", round(mean(((pr0$p_left > 0.5) == (pr0$Diff > 0))[pr0$Diff != 0]), 3), "\n")
cat("observed accuracy:                 ", round(mean(pas$Correct), 3), "\n")
cat("trials dropped for an unhovered box:", prep_cond$n_dropped, "of", nrow(pas), "\n")
```

```{r sanity-signs}
# Sign patterns from the regression on simulated choices, hand-set parameters
# (sigma = 5 points per second for everyone).
sanity <- list(
  "Per-condition prior, q = 0.5"               = list(variant = variants$cond_lam1, par = list(s0 = 1, q = 0.5,  lambda = 1)),
  "Per-condition prior, q = 0.14"              = list(variant = variants$cond_lam1, par = list(s0 = 1, q = 0.14, lambda = 1)),
  "Per-condition prior, q = 0.14, lambda = 2.5" = list(variant = variants$cond_lam,  par = list(s0 = 1, q = 0.14, lambda = 2.5)),
  "Zero prior"                                 = list(variant = variants$zero,      par = list(s0 = 1, q = 0.5,  lambda = 1)),
  "Flat prior"                                 = list(variant = variants$flat,      par = list(s0 = 1e3, q = 0.5, lambda = 1))
)
for (nm in names(sanity)) {
  sp   <- sanity[[nm]]
  prep <- prepare_boxes(boxlong, sp$variant)
  tr   <- choice_probabilities(prep, sig_five, sp$par)
  sw   <- simulated_weights(tr, reps = 5)
  cat("\n==", nm, "==\n")
  for (tt in c("N", "B", "P")) {
    w <- sw$weights %>% filter(Study == 2, WN == "Narrow", type == tt) %>% arrange(value)
    cat(sprintf("  %s (Study 2, Narrow): %s   crossover = %s\n", tt,
                paste(sprintf("%+.2f", w$estimate), collapse = " "), crossover(w$value, w$estimate)))
  }
}
```

# Parameter recovery

Run by `code/parameter_recovery/recover_bayesian_attributes.R` (20 simulated
datasets on the real trial structure, true $q$, shared $\lambda$ and
per-subject noise drawn at random, refit from scratch with the same procedure).
The notebook only shows the cached results.

```{r recovery, fig.width=2 * .figw, fig.height=2 * .figh}
recovery_file <- file.path(cache_dir, "parameter_recovery.rds")
if (!file.exists(recovery_file)) {
  cat("No parameter-recovery cache. Run: Rscript code/parameter_recovery/recover_bayesian_attributes.R\n")
} else {
  rec <- readRDS(recovery_file)
  sig_df <- tibble(); grp_df <- tibble()
  for (r in rec) { sig_df <- bind_rows(sig_df, r$sigma); grp_df <- bind_rows(grp_df, r$group) }
  cat("datasets:", length(rec), "\n")
  for (s in 1:2) {
    x <- sig_df %>% filter(Study == s)
    cat(sprintf("sigma, Study %d: r(log) = %.3f, median |relative error| = %.3f\n", s,
                cor(log(x$true), log(x$recovered)), median(abs(x$recovered - x$true) / x$true)))
  }
  cat(sprintf("q:  r = %.3f, median |recovered - true| = %.3f\n",
              cor(grp_df$true_q, grp_df$rec_q), median(abs(grp_df$rec_q - grp_df$true_q))))
  lam_df <- grp_df %>% filter(WN == "Narrow")   # lambda is shared: one point per dataset
  cat(sprintf("lambda: r(log) = %.3f, median |log(recovered / true)| = %.3f\n",
              cor(log(lam_df$true_lambda), log(lam_df$rec_lambda)), median(abs(log(lam_df$rec_lambda / lam_df$true_lambda)))))

  # The paper's figure, drawn by code/utilities/plot_parameter_recovery.R and
  # saved to paper/figures by the recovery script.
  print(plot_parameter_recovery(sig_df, grp_df))
}
```

# Fits and leave-one-out

Every variant is fit to all trials on the profile likelihood (noise per
subject re-optimised on a grid of $q$, then $q$ per range condition and
$\lambda$ refined, jointly over both conditions when $\lambda$ is shared), then
refit 60 times leaving out the $k$-th trial of every subject and predicting it.
Every fold is fit from scratch by the same three stages on the training trials,
with the shrinkage centre recomputed from them, so nothing from the full fit
enters a fold. The zero and flat priors go through the same stages with $q$
fixed at 0.5: a single noise pass, nothing to refine per condition, and a
bounded one-dimensional search over $\lambda$ with the noise re-optimised at
every candidate. The caches come from `code/fitting/run_bayesian_fits.R`.

```{r fits}
runs <- list()
for (name in names(variants)) {
  have_cache <- file.exists(file.path(cache_dir, paste0("fit_", name, ".rds"))) &&
                file.exists(file.path(cache_dir, paste0("loo_", name, ".rds")))
  if (!have_cache && !RUN_FITS) { cat("No cache for", name, "and RUN_FITS is FALSE. Skipping.\n"); next }
  runs[[name]] <- run_variant(name, boxlong, cache_dir, verbose = FALSE)
}
names(runs)
```

Convergence: Nelder-Mead stops when the relative spread of the objective over
the simplex falls below $10^{-7}$ (code 0) or at the cap on function
evaluations (code 1). The full fit's code(s) and the number of folds with a
nonzero code, per variant; the variants with no Nelder-Mead call (only
one-dimensional bounded searches) show "none".

```{r convergence}
conv <- tibble()
for (name in names(runs)) {
  f  <- runs[[name]]$fit
  fp <- runs[[name]]$loo$fold_params
  conv <- bind_rows(conv, tibble(
    variant = name,
    full_fit = if (length(f$convergence) > 0) paste(f$convergence, collapse = " ") else "none",
    folds = n_distinct(fp$fold),
    folds_not_converged = n_distinct(fp$fold[fp$convergence != 0])
  ))
}
as.data.frame(conv)
```

## Parameters

```{r params}
params <- tibble()
for (name in names(runs)) {
  f <- runs[[name]]$fit
  params <- bind_rows(params, tibble(
    variant = name, label = variants[[name]]$label, range = names(f$s0),
    s0 = unname(f$s0), q = unname(f$q[names(f$s0)]), lambda = unname(f$lambda[names(f$s0)]),
    nll = f$nll, sigma_median = median(f$sigma), sigma_iqr_lo = quantile(f$sigma, 0.25), sigma_iqr_hi = quantile(f$sigma, 0.75)
  ))
}
# The reference in points: the prior reference's minimum plus q times its range.
ref_pts <- tibble()
for (name in names(runs)) {
  v <- variants[[name]]
  if (v$prior != "fitted") next
  rd <- reference_distributions(boxlong, v$prior_ref) %>% distinct(WN, type, min, max)
  f  <- runs[[name]]$fit
  ref_pts <- bind_rows(ref_pts, rd %>% mutate(variant = name, q = unname(f$q[as.character(WN)]), reference = min + q * (max - min)) %>%
                         select(variant, WN, type, reference))
}
params %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3))) %>% as.data.frame()
ref_pts %>% pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = reference) %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 1))) %>% as.data.frame()
```

## Out-of-sample log-likelihood

Held-out log-likelihood per model: the sum over every trial of the log
probability the model gave to the choice that was made, from a fit that did
not see that trial. Differences from the main model (`cond_lam`) are summarised
across subjects (one number per subject = that subject's summed difference).

```{r loo-summary}
loo_ll <- tibble()
for (name in names(runs)) {
  p <- runs[[name]]$loo$pred
  loo_ll <- bind_rows(loo_ll, tibble(variant = name, Study = p$Study, Subject = p$Subject, WN = p$WN,
                                     Trial = p$Trial, ChooseL = p$ChooseL, ll = heldout_loglik(p)))
}
loo_total <- loo_ll %>% group_by(variant) %>%
  summarise(total_ll = sum(ll), per_trial = mean(ll), n_trials = n(), .groups = "drop")
loo_cells <- loo_ll %>% group_by(variant, Study, WN) %>%
  summarise(per_trial = mean(ll), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(Study, WN), values_from = per_trial, names_prefix = "S")

subj_ll <- loo_ll %>% group_by(variant, Subject) %>% summarise(ll = sum(ll), .groups = "drop")
ref_ll  <- subj_ll %>% filter(variant == "cond_lam") %>% select(Subject, ll_ref = ll)
loo_diff <- subj_ll %>% left_join(ref_ll, by = "Subject") %>% mutate(d = ll - ll_ref) %>%
  group_by(variant) %>%
  summarise(diff_total = sum(d), diff_mean = mean(d), diff_se = sd(d) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")

loo_table <- loo_total %>% left_join(loo_cells, by = "variant") %>% left_join(loo_diff, by = "variant") %>%
  mutate(label = sapply(variant, function(v) variants[[v]]$label)) %>%
  relocate(label, .after = variant)
loo_table %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 4))) %>% as.data.frame()
```

# Out-of-sample attention weights

For every plotted variant, ten simulated choices per trial are drawn from the
held-out probabilities and pushed through the cell-weight regression (plain
logistic regression per range condition and study). The data's weights come
from the paper's brms fits; the data's value slopes in the table below come from
the same plain regression as the models, so like is compared with like.

```{r oos-weights}
plotted <- c("cond_lam", "cond_lam1", "type_lam", "type_lam1", "zero", "flat")
weights_model <- list()
slopes_model  <- list()
for (name in plotted) {
  if (is.null(runs[[name]])) next
  tr <- runs[[name]]$loo$pred %>% transmute(Subject, Trial, WN, Study, p_left = p_left_heldout)
  sw <- simulated_weights(tr, reps = 10, seed = 1)
  weights_model[[name]] <- sw$weights
  slopes_model[[name]]  <- sw$slopes
}

# The data through the same regression (for the slope table).
sw_data <- cell_weight_glm(boxlong %>% mutate(TrialKey = Trial), pas %>% mutate(TrialKey = Trial))
```

## Main figure: data and the best model

The paper gets two figures: this one (the data and the per-condition prior
with loss aversion) and one supplementary figure (the per-condition prior
without loss aversion, the per-type prior with loss aversion, the zero prior,
the flat prior). The other comparisons below are shown here but not saved.

```{r fig-main, fig.width=2 * .figw, fig.height=2 * .figh}
# Rows of data and model weights -> a (rows x studies) figure. The first row's
# titles carry the study ("Study 1" over "Data"); later rows just carry their
# label. With a `name`, saved under that name in paper/figures and
# notebooks/notebook_figures; without one, only drawn.
weights_figure <- function(rows, name = NULL, ylim = c(-0.5, 0.5)) {
  panels <- list()
  for (row in names(rows)) {
    for (s in 1:2) {
      w <- rows[[row]]
      title <- if (row == names(rows)[1]) paste0("Study ", s, "\n", row) else row
      panels[[paste(row, s)]] <- if (is.null(w) || nrow(w) == 0) plot_spacer() else
        plot_weights_by_range(w %>% filter(Study == s), title = title, ylim = ylim)
    }
  }
  fig <- wrap_plots(panels, ncol = 2) + plot_layout(guides = "collect")
  if (!is.null(name)) {
    ggsave(file.path(fig_dir,    paste0(name, ".pdf")), fig, width = 2 * .figw, height = length(rows) * .figh)
    ggsave(file.path(nb_fig_dir, paste0(name, ".pdf")), fig, width = 2 * .figw, height = length(rows) * .figh)
  }
  fig
}

weights_figure(list("Data" = weights_data,
                    "Bayesian Model" = weights_model$cond_lam),
               "bayesian_model")
```

The data row is repeated so the reader can compare without flipping back to
the main figure. The second row is the main model with $\lambda = 1$: without

Every other model row has $\lambda$ fitted.

```{r fig-supp, fig.width=2 * .figw, fig.height=5 * .figh}

                    "Per-condition prior, no loss aversion" = weights_model$cond_lam1,
                    "Per-type prior" = weights_model$type_lam,

```

```{r dip-table}
# Attention weight at the lowest aversive value of each range condition
# (Narrow -30, Wide -50), by study, for the data, the main model and the main
# model without loss aversion: the comparison the figure's second row is for.
dip_rows <- list("Data"                            = weights_data,
                 "Per-condition prior"             = weights_model$cond_lam,
                 "Per-condition prior, lambda = 1" = weights_model$cond_lam1)
dip <- tibble()
for (nm in names(dip_rows)) {
  w <- dip_rows[[nm]]
  if (is.null(w) || nrow(w) == 0) next
  lowest <- w %>% filter(type == "N") %>%
    group_by(Study, WN) %>% slice_min(value, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup()
  dip <- bind_rows(dip, lowest %>% transmute(source = nm, Study, WN, value, estimate, lo, hi))
}
# One weight from the table, formatted (for the notes).
dip_at <- function(src, s, rng) {
  x <- dip %>% filter(source == src, Study == s, WN == rng)
  if (nrow(x) == 0) "NA" else sprintf("%.2f", x$estimate)
}
dip %>% arrange(Study, WN, source) %>% mutate(across(c(estimate, lo, hi), \(x) round(x, 3))) %>% as.data.frame()
```

## Crossovers and value slopes

Where each type's weights cross zero (fraction of the type's range), and the
value slopes (log-odds per 10 points) with their Wide / Narrow ratio. Every
variant reproduces a drop from Narrow to Wide through the fitted per-subject
noise, so the ratio itself does not separate them. What does is the weighting of
B against P and N within a condition: per-type units predict a B/P slope ratio
of 0.79 in Narrow and 1.20 in Wide, points predict 1 in both.

```{r slopes}
# Crossovers: the data (brms, and through the same glm as the models) and every
# model (glm on held-out simulations).
cross <- crossover_table(weights_data, "Data (brms)")
cross <- bind_rows(cross, crossover_table(sw_data$weights, "Data (glm)"))
for (name in names(weights_model)) cross <- bind_rows(cross, crossover_table(weights_model[[name]], variants[[name]]$label))
cross_wide <- cross %>% pivot_wider(names_from = c(WN), values_from = crossover) %>% arrange(Study, type, source)
as.data.frame(cross_wide)

# Value slopes: data (same glm) and every model.
slope_tbl <- sw_data$slopes %>% mutate(source = "Data (glm)")
for (name in names(slopes_model)) slope_tbl <- bind_rows(slope_tbl, slopes_model[[name]] %>% mutate(source = variants[[name]]$label))
slope_wide <- slope_tbl %>% select(source, Study, type, WN, estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = WN, values_from = estimate) %>%
  mutate(ratio = Wide / Narrow) %>%
  left_join(cross_wide %>% rename(cross_Narrow = Narrow, cross_Wide = Wide), by = c("source", "Study", "type")) %>%
  arrange(Study, type, source)
slope_wide %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3))) %>% as.data.frame()
```

## Text Output

Statistics quoted in the paper's model sections, as LaTeX math snippets in
`paper/text_output/` (same convention as the main notebook: a study or a
between-study contrast goes in the subscript, everything else in the
superscript), plus a compact model-comparison table for the paper.

```{r text-output}
text_dir  <- file.path(paths$root, paths$paper_text)
save_text <- function(text, name) {
  write.text(text, file.path(text_dir, paste0(name, ".tex")))
  cat(name, ": ", text, "\n")
}
fmt_delta <- function(a, b) {
  # Held-out log-likelihood of variant a minus variant b: total, and mean +/- SE per participant.
  x  <- subj_ll %>% filter(variant %in% c(a, b)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = variant, values_from = ll)
  dd <- x[[a]] - x[[b]]
  sprintf("%.0f\\ (%.2f \\pm %.2f \\text{ per participant})", sum(dd), mean(dd), sd(dd) / sqrt(length(dd)))
}

best <- runs$cond_lam$fit
save_text(sprintf("$q^{\\text{Narrow}} = %.2f$, $q^{\\text{Wide}} = %.2f$, $\\lambda = %.2f$",
                  best$q[["Narrow"]], best$q[["Wide"]], best$lambda[[1]]),
          "bayes_best_params")
rp <- ref_pts %>% filter(variant == "cond_lam", type == "P")
save_text(sprintf("$%.0f$ points in Narrow and $%.0f$ points in Wide", rp$reference[rp$WN == "Narrow"], rp$reference[rp$WN == "Wide"]), "bayes_best_reference")
save_text(sprintf("$\\lambda^{\\text{Narrow}} = %.2f$, $\\lambda^{\\text{Wide}} = %.2f$", runs$cond_lamcond$fit$lambda[["Narrow"]], runs$cond_lamcond$fit$lambda[["Wide"]]), "bayes_lambda_by_range")
save_text(paste0("$\\Delta^{\\text{loss aversion - none}} = ", fmt_delta("cond_lam", "cond_lam1"), "$"), "bayes_loo_lambda")
save_text(paste0("$\\Delta^{\\text{per-condition - per-type}} = ", fmt_delta("cond_lam", "type_lam"), "$"), "bayes_loo_prior")
save_text(paste0("$\\Delta^{\\text{per-condition - flat}} = ", fmt_delta("cond_lam", "flat"), "$, ",
                 "$\\Delta^{\\text{per-condition - zero}} = ", fmt_delta("cond_lam", "zero"), "$"), "bayes_loo_flat_zero")
if (exists("grp_df")) {
  # Pearson r between true and recovered values, all on the linear scale; sigma
  # by study (one point per participant and dataset), q over both range
  # conditions, lambda over datasets.
  r_sigma <- c()
  for (s in 1:2) {
    x <- sig_df %>% filter(Study == s)
    r_sigma[s] <- cor(x$true, x$recovered)
  }
  save_text(sprintf("$r^{q} = %.2f$, $r^{\\lambda} = %.2f$, $r^{\\sigma}_{\\text{Study 1}} = %.2f$, $r^{\\sigma}_{\\text{Study 2}} = %.2f$",
                    cor(grp_df$true_q, grp_df$rec_q), cor(lam_df$true_lambda, lam_df$rec_lambda), r_sigma[1], r_sigma[2]),
            "bayes_recovery")
}
save_text(sprintf("%s", format(prep_cond$n_dropped, big.mark = ",")), "bayes_dropped_trials")
# Held-out trials of the main model whose chosen option got a probability below
# the 1e-12 floor applied in heldout_loglik (errors on easy trials).
p_main   <- runs$cond_lam$loo$pred
p_chosen <- ifelse(p_main$ChooseL == 1, p_main$p_left_heldout, 1 - p_main$p_left_heldout)
save_text(sprintf("%d of %s", sum(p_chosen < 1e-12), format(nrow(p_main), big.mark = ",")), "bayes_clipped_trials")

# Compact comparison table for the paper: the four priors with lambda fitted
# plus the main model without loss aversion.
comp <- tibble()
for (name in c("cond_lam", "cond_lam1", "type_lam", "zero", "flat")) {
  f <- runs[[name]]$fit
  x <- subj_ll %>% filter(variant %in% c(name, "cond_lam")) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = variant, values_from = ll)
  dd <- if (name == "cond_lam") rep(0, nrow(x)) else x[[name]] - x[["cond_lam"]]
  comp <- bind_rows(comp, tibble(
    Prior = c(cond_lam = "Per condition", cond_lam1 = "Per condition", type_lam = "Per type", zero = "Zero", flat = "Flat")[[name]],
    `$\\lambda$` = if (f$variant$lambda == "fixed1") "1 (fixed)" else sprintf("%.2f", f$lambda[[1]]),
    `$q$ (N/W)`   = if (f$variant$prior == "fitted") sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", f$q[["Narrow"]], f$q[["Wide"]]) else "--",
    `Out-of-Sample LL` = sprintf("%.0f", sum(loo_ll$ll[loo_ll$variant == name])),
    `$\\Delta$ per subject (SE)` = if (name == "cond_lam") "--" else sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(dd), sd(dd) / sqrt(length(dd)))
  ))
}
tex <- kable(comp, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = "")
writeLines(as.character(tex), file.path(tab_dir, "bayesian_model_comparison.tex"))
cat(as.character(tex), "\n")
```

# Notes

Fourth run, 2026-10-29 (evening): $\lambda$ fitted in every variant by the
same algorithm. The zero and flat priors fix $q$ at 0.5 (an objective 0 for
these symmetric spans) and fit $\sigma$ and $\lambda$; the main model, its
caches and every snippet about it are unchanged. The zero prior fits
$\lambda = `r sprintf("%.2f", runs$zero$fit$lambda[[1]])`$ and the flat prior
$\lambda = `r sprintf("%.2f", runs$flat$fit$lambda[[1]])`$. A $\lambda$ below 1
under the flat prior means that, with no pull toward a prior, the kink at zero
is used to flatten value sensitivity on the aversive side (the data's N value
slope is a little shallower than P's), not to amplify repulsion. Out of sample
the main model beats the zero prior by
`r sprintf("%.0f", sum(loo_ll$ll[loo_ll$variant == "cond_lam"]) - sum(loo_ll$ll[loo_ll$variant == "zero"]))`
units and the flat prior by
`r sprintf("%.0f", sum(loo_ll$ll[loo_ll$variant == "cond_lam"]) - sum(loo_ll$ll[loo_ll$variant == "flat"]))`
(third run, with $\lambda = 1$ in both: 329 and 431). Fitting $\lambda$ thus
cost both priors about 40 held-out units while gaining them 47 and 41 in
sample: the loss sits in four subjects whose noise shrank by up to a quarter
under $\lambda < 1$, so a held-out error cost them more; half of the subjects
gain and the median trial is unchanged. The supplementary figure
gained the main model with $\lambda = 1$ as its second row, and the paper's
comparison table dropped the per-type $\lambda = 1$ row. At the lowest aversive
value of Study 2 Narrow ($-30$) the data's weight is
`r dip_at("Data", 2, "Narrow")`, the main model's
`r dip_at("Per-condition prior", 2, "Narrow")` and the $\lambda = 1$ model's
`r dip_at("Per-condition prior, lambda = 1", 2, "Narrow")` (Study 2 Wide, $-50$:
`r dip_at("Data", 2, "Wide")`, `r dip_at("Per-condition prior", 2, "Wide")`,
`r dip_at("Per-condition prior, lambda = 1", 2, "Wide")`); the fitted $\lambda$
of 1.07 is a 7 percent amplification, so the two model rows differ by
hundredths and both undershoot the data.

Third full run, 2026-10-29: prior spread fixed at the spread of the reference
distribution ($s_p = s_D$), partial pooling of the per-subject noise, loss
aversion, 60-fold leave-one-out (folds warm-started from the full fit, since
replaced; see the fourth run), 20 recovery datasets.

**Headline.** The best partial-pooling model has one reference per range
condition at $q = 0.19$ (Narrow) and $0.15$ (Wide), i.e. $-19$ and $-35$
points, inside the aversive range; and a shared loss-aversion coefficient of
1.07 (per condition: 1.13 in Narrow, 1.01 in Wide, 8 held-out units better than
the shared value). It beats the same prior without loss aversion by 41 held-out
log-likelihood units (0.03 per subject, SE 0.01), the per-type prior with loss
aversion by 203 (0.14 per subject, SE 0.04), the zero prior by 329 and the flat
prior by 431. Fixing the prior spread cost the per-condition prior 16
in-sample units relative to its free-spread fit (which had found 1.07 / 1.17),
but cost the per-type prior 174, because that prior had wanted to be twice as
wide as its reference; this is why the gap between the two priors is now much
larger than in the previous run.

**Out-of-sample attention weights (main model).** The N crossovers sit at 0.26
to 0.41 of the range (data 0.28 to 0.34); the weights rise monotonically with
value in every type; P and B are mostly positive; the Wide/Narrow slope ratios
are close to the data's. The repulsion at the bottom of the N range is about
70 percent of the data's (Study 2 Narrow, $-30$: model $-0.12$, data $-0.17$).
Not reproduced: the dip in the lower-middle of the P range next to the steep
rise at the top (every P box attracts in the model), the all-positive B
weights of Study 2 Narrow with the spike at $+5$, and the underweighting of B
relative to P in Narrow.

**Why loss aversion stays small.** The hand-set example in the sanity checks
shows that $\lambda = 2.5$ at this reference produces $-0.50$ at $-30$, far more
than the data's $-0.17$, so the mechanism is not weak. The likelihood holds
$\lambda$ down because the kink also steepens choice sensitivity among
below-reference values, and the data's aversive value slope is no steeper than
the appetitive one.

**Parameter recovery.** Twenty datasets on the real trial structure with noise
drawn in the fitted range (2 to 25 points per second) and the prior spread
fixed as in the fit. $q$ comes back with $r = 0.996$ (median error 0.009),
$\lambda$ with $r = 0.98$ on the log scale (median error 1 percent), and the
per-subject noise with $r$ of 0.85 to 0.90. Fixing the spread removed the
unidentified cases of the previous run, where a weak true prior had let $q$
and $\lambda$ wander.

**Next steps.** A per-type $q$ inside the per-condition model, since the P dip
and the B pattern suggest P's reference sits higher than N's; a free weight for
B; a sampling-policy module for the $+5$ cells; then port to `Main_Analysis.Rmd`.

Fourth full run, 2026-10-30: same model and settings as the third run, but
every leave-one-out fold is now fit from scratch by the full three-stage
procedure on its training trials (grid, refinement, Nelder-Mead, shrinkage
centre) instead of one warm-started round from the full fit; the lapse-rate
variant and all lapse code removed; Nelder-Mead convergence codes recorded.

**Headline.** The full-data fits are unchanged (same code path): $q = 0.19$ /
$0.15$, $\lambda = 1.07$, in-sample NLL 28328.6. The from-scratch folds lower
the held-out log-likelihood of every variant by 3.5 to 16.8 units (the warm
start had let a little of each held-out trial leak into the group parameters
through the full-fit $\sigma$'s), and the ranking is unchanged: main model
$-30968$; without loss aversion $-31002$ ($-34$); per-type prior $-31174$
($-206$); zero prior $-31327$ ($-359$); flat prior $-31428$ ($-460$); $\lambda$
per condition $-30963$ ($+5$; 1.13 Narrow, 1.01 Wide). Across the main model's
60 folds $q$ ranges 0.16 to 0.20 (Narrow) and 0.14 to 0.16 (Wide) and $\lambda$
1.07 to 1.09. Nelder-Mead stopped on its tolerance in the full fit and in all
60 folds of every variant (the `convergence` chunk). The $10^{-12}$ floor on
held-out probabilities binds on 5 of the main model's 58,122 trials; 26 trials
sit below $10^{-6}$ and together make up 1.8 percent of its held-out
log-likelihood. Four processes from 00:28 to 03:59; the main model alone took
3.4 minutes per fold with the other three running.
